abstract: This contribution presents a new concept for depth acquisition in post-production and visual effects (vfx) creation. The main idea is to mount two satellite cameras to the left and the right of an electronic D-cinema camera such that the whole rig forms a trinocular camera setup. Based on this system, depth is estimated by robust stereo matching and the trifocal constraint is exploited to determine the accuracy of the depth values. The information is calculated almost in realtime and can be directly previewed at the set. This paper explains the concept in more detail and describes the basic image processing algorithms. Finally, the theoretically achievable depth accuracy is discussed and results of the first experiments based on computer simulations are presented.

authors.bio: Ralf Tanger graduated with a degree in electrical engineering from the Technical University of Berlin in 1996. From 1993 to 1997 he worked for Daimler-Benz Research in the field of image classification with neural networks. In 1997, he joined the Image Processing department of the Fraunhofer Institute for Telecommunications, Heinrich-Hertz-Institute (FhG/HHI) in Berlin, Germany. He was engaged in several European and German research projects, mainly in the field of segmentation and video conferencing. Since 2002, he has been project manager. Currently, he is mainly interested in 3-D video analysis, large-scale system integration, and realtime processing. Tanger is a member of IEEE and VDI.
authors.name: R. Tanger

authors.bio: Nicole Atzpadin, nee Brandenburg, was born in Berlin, Germany in August 1973. She received a diploma degree in electrical engineering from the Technical University of Berlin, Germany, in May 2000. Since 1998, Atzpadin has been working in the Image Processing department of the Heinrich-Hertz-Institute. She first worked as a student in the field of disparity estimation. Since receiving her diploma degree she works as a research assistant on the DFG project 3-DEvi, where she is engaged in research for 3-D analysis, novel view synthesis, and realtime video conferencing. After a parental leave in 2003 to 2004, Atzpadin was self-employed and developed algorithms in the context of 3-D analysis for cinema post-production.
authors.name: N. Atzpadin

authors.bio: Marcus Müller received a diploma degree in computer science from the Technical University, Berlin, Germany, in 2004. Since 2001, he has been working in the Image Processing department, Fraunhofer Institute for Telecommunications HHI. He began working there as a student assistant, on color-segmentation and disparity estimation, in a two-year DFG project called VITA. Since receiving his diploma degree he has been working as a research assistant on several projects concerning stereo and multi-view-analysis, depth estimation, and novel view synthesis. Müller is now working on a PhD thesis on future 3-D-TV services.
authors.name: M. Müller

authors.bio: Christoph Fehn received a diploma degree (MS) in electrical engineering from the University of Dortmund, Germany, in 1998. Since then, he has been with the Fraunhofer Institute for Telecommunications HHI, where he is currently working as a scientific project manager and coordinator for projects in the area of immersive media, three-dimensional television (3DTV), and digital cinema. In 2006, he received a PhD degree from the Technical University Berlin, Germany, for his work on a novel approach for 3-DTV. Fehn is a member of VDE, SMPTE, and IEEE and has been an active contributor to the ISO MPEG group, where he is acting as an associate editor of the new MPEG-C Part 3 standard, which is concerned with the definition of encoding and transport mechanisms for depth/parallax data or other auxiliary video data representations.
authors.name: C. Fehn

authors.affiliation: The Immersive Media & 3D Video Group at the Fraunhofer Institute for Telecommunications HHI
authors.bio: Peter Kauff is head of the Immersive Media & 3D Video Group at the Fraunhofer Institute for Telecommunications HHI. He received a Dipl.-Ing. degree in electrical engineering and telecommunications from the Technical University of Aachen, Germany, in 1984. He has been with the Heinrich-Hertz-Institute since then, involved in numerous German and European projects related to digital HDTV signal processing and coding, interactive MPEG-4-based services, as well as a number of projects related to advanced 3-D video processing for immersive tele-presence and immersive media. Kauff has been engaged in several European research projects, such as Eureka 95, Race-project Flash, Acts-project Hamlet, COST211ter&quad, Esprit-Project Nemesis, IST-Projects Virtue and Attest, and the Presence Working Group of IST-FET Proactive Initiative.
authors.name: P. Kauff

authors.bio: Carsten Herpel holds a Dipl.-Ing. degree in communications engineering from RWTH Aachen, Germany. He is a senior technical advisor in the production workflow lab at Thomson's research facility in Hannover. His past expertise covers video compression, where he contributed to the MPEG-1 and −2 standards; multimedia system architecture (co-editor of MPEG-4 and −7 specifications), as well as logical formats for disk-based media (Blu-ray disk, HD-DVD). Currently, Herpel leads a project contributing to the evolution of workflows and infrastructure for high-end digital media production and post-production towards higher fidelity and 3-D.
authors.name: C. Herpel
